winner.hypothesis: Adding an outer non-structural skip to LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts, outside-string path just before `const b = buf[i];` at L283) that, driven by a module-level Uint8Array(256) class table WCLS marking only '"' '{' '[' '}' ']' '\n' ' ' '\t' '\r' as 1, advances i over every run of class-0 bytes in one tight do/while (setting lineHasContent = true once per run) will raise the primary speedup from ~1.50 to ~1.62-1.68, because on top of the round-2 string loop the outside-string bytes are now a large share of cost and every class-0 byte currently pays a full outer iteration + inString test + switch dispatch only to set lineHasContent = true. Unlike round 2's failed skipLHC it is not gated on lineHasContent and whitespace is folded into the table, so it skips digits/true/false/null/':'/',' runs everywhere with no extra guard. This is the only change: the string branch, the switch cases, checkpoint modulo, record pushes, for-await loop, Buffer.from conversion and EOF handling are untouched.

losers.hypothesis: Replacing the 4x-unrolled byte reject inside the string-skip loop of LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts L256-263 on 2fb4bdc) with an aligned Uint32Array SWAR word loop that tests each 4-byte word for a 0x22 or 0x5c lane via the haszero trick ((v - 0x01010101) & ~v & 0x80808080 on v = x ^ 0x22222222 and v = x ^ 0x5c5c5c5c), with the existing byte path kept as the unaligned head/tail and hit-word fallback, will raise the primary speedup from ~1.50 to ~1.55-1.60 (~1.05x relative), because it checks 4 string bytes per typed-array load with one combined branch instead of 4 loads and 4 compares, and it never stops on in-string bytes <= 0x5c other than quote/backslash. Chosen over rej4u32 (brief idea 3) because swarU32 has the higher median alone (~1.055 vs ~1.048 relative, its one low reading 1.014 came from a loaded process at 494 MB/s real build) and the better stack with the outer skip (1.21-1.24 vs 1.19-1.21), and its stop set is exactly the two bytes that change state, so it stays fast on real-world strings with spaces/digits/punctuation, where rej4u32 drops to the byte path. This is the only change: the escaped-carry branch, the byte tail, the outside-string switch, checkpoint modulo, record pushes, for-await loop, Buffer.from conversion and EOF handling are untouched.
